text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- The government plans a 54 percent increase of wages to cushion the impact of inflation, the paper says.
- Price of newsprint to increase by 54 percent.
- The central bank will tighten control on commercial banks, the paper says.
- Trade unions threatened with labour unrest to protest against government's failure to present a coherent social protection programme.
- The state budget affected by failure of Romanian to cash some 1.0 trillion lei from exports performed in 1996, the paper says.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Foreign companies could invest over $10 billion in Romania, the paper quotes Romanian Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea as saying.
- Private DAC Air airline will start flights to Italy, the paper says.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Romania's economic reforms cannot succeed without support from a strong banking system, the paper says.
- Steel plant in Galati owes the state budget some 500 billion lei.
- Trade unions in telecommunications sector oppose privatisation of Romtelecom RA telephone utility, the paper says.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Romania's Tarom SA state-run airline plans to open Eastern Europe's biggest training centre for airline pilots.
General:
ADEVARUL
- U.S.' FBI expected to open office in Bucharest next year.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Italy supports Romania's efforts to integrate into NATO and EU, Italian ambassador to Bucharest Giuseppe de Michelis says in interview. ($=6,376)
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
